title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Anglo-Indian spiced rice with smoked haddock and boiled eggs
excerpt: Kedgeree is one of the great British colonial dishes: spiced rice cooked with flaked smoked haddock, hard-boiled eggs, curry powder, and butter. It began as an adaptation of the Indian dish khichri (lentils and rice) and was transformed into the breakfast and brunch dish eaten across Victorian Britain. It is now eaten at any meal and is deeply satisfying any time of day.
sourceNotes: Kedgeree was developed by British colonists in India as an adaptation of khichri, the Indian dish of spiced lentils and rice. It was brought back to Britain in the 18th century and became a standard Victorian breakfast dish, particularly popular as part of the country house breakfast spread. The fish, eggs, and spiced rice combination is now eaten at any meal.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The rice can be cooked ahead and chilled. Assemble quickly to serve.

content.text: Poach the haddock in milk first -- the fish cooks through and the poaching milk can be used to cook the rice. This gives the rice the smoked fish flavour without adding it separately. The eggs should be soft-boiled with a jammy yolk rather than hard-boiled -- 7 minutes in boiling water gives a golden, just-set yolk.

items.prepNote: add to taste -- the fish is salty

content.text: Poach {{smoked-haddock}} haddock in {{whole-milk}} milk for 8 minutes until just cooked. Remove the fish. Strain and reserve the milk. Flake the fish into large chunks, discarding skin and bones. Boil {{eggs}} eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water, and peel. Halve and set aside.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} butter in a wide pan. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes until softened and golden. Add {{garlic}} garlic, {{curry-powder}} curry powder, and {{turmeric-ground}} turmeric. Stir for 1 minute. Add {{basmati-rice}} rice and stir to coat.

Add the reserved poaching milk plus enough water to make 700 ml total. Bring to a boil, reduce to the lowest simmer, cover, and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes. Gently fold in the flaked {{smoked-haddock}} fish. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Top with halved {{eggs}} eggs, {{parsley-flat}} parsley, and {{lemon}} lemon wedges.

items.symptom: The rice is stodgy and clumped together
items.cause: Too much liquid, or the rice was stirred during cooking.
items.fix: Spread the cooked rice on a tray and leave to steam for 5 minutes -- this separates the grains. Never stir rice during cooking or it releases starch and clumps. Use exactly 700 ml liquid for 300 g rice.

content.text: Kedgeree began as a British adaptation of khichri, a simple Indian dish of spiced lentils and rice, during the period of British rule in India. Returned colonists brought it to Britain in the 18th century, where it was adapted with smoked haddock (readily available in Britain) and eggs. By the Victorian period it was a standard breakfast dish in upper-class households. It is now eaten across Britain at any time of day.
